_comment: JINGLE FORMS AND CHARACTERS. A jingle is not a genre and not a loop, which is why briefs like 'a jingle for the Absurd News Cartoon Show' fell through LoopStar's 24-style matcher and produced a generic 4-chord vamp. A jingle is a SHORT THROUGH-COMPOSED PIECE with a beginning, a hook, and an ending it stops on. Its identity comes from FUNCTION (what it punctuates), CHARACTER (what it sounds like it is about) and INSTRUMENTATION — not from a genre. Both vocabularies live here so they can grow by PR with no rebuild (RULE #1).

forms.name: Button
forms.blurb: The full stop. One accent, held, then silence. What ends a segment.

forms.name: Sting
forms.blurb: One gesture and a stop. Scene transitions, reveals, punchlines.

forms.name: Logo
forms.blurb: An identity motif — three to five notes you could hum back. Sparse; the notes carry it, not the groove.

forms.name: Bumper
forms.blurb: In and out of a break. States the hook once, answers it, stops.

forms.name: Theme
forms.blurb: A show's front title: sets up, states the hook, answers it, lifts, lands.

_sectionRoles.intro: Sets the key and the pulse. Thinner than the hook — it is a runway.
_sectionRoles.gesture: A single rising or falling figure. The whole point of a sting.
_sectionRoles.motif: The identity cell: 3-5 notes with one leap. Repeatable, hummable, no groove needed.
_sectionRoles.hook: The memorable phrase. Densest melodic writing; everything else supports it.
_sectionRoles.answer: The hook's reply — same rhythm, different contour, or the same contour a step away.
_sectionRoles.lift: One bar of rising tension into the button. Often a fill or a held dominant.
_sectionRoles.button: The ending. An accent on beat 1, held and allowed to ring. NOTHING after it.

characters.name: Fanfare
characters.blurb: Brass and dotted rhythms. Signals importance before a word is spoken.

characters.name: Cartoon
characters.blurb: Xylophone, pizzicato and muted brass. Light, staccato, fast-moving.

characters.name: Absurd
characters.blurb: An instrument with no business being there, and a resolution that goes somewhere wrong. A modifier more than a character — it colours whatever it is combined with.

characters.name: Corporate
characters.blurb: Bells and warm pads. Confident, resolved, nothing surprising.

characters.name: Sports
characters.blurb: Brass over taiko. Big, square, built for a crowd.

characters.name: Retro game
characters.blurb: Square and saw leads. Fast, bright, unapologetically synthetic.

characters.name: Mystery
characters.blurb: Low strings and vibraphone, minor and unresolved until the very last hit.

characters.name: Warm
characters.blurb: Acoustic guitar and vibraphone. Unhurried, major, nothing to prove.

_defaults.note: A brief matching no character still gets a real jingle rather than a failure — corporate is the least-wrong neutral, and the reply always says which character was inferred so the caller can correct it.
